questions.text: एक व्यक्ति जिसके पिता वर्णांध थे, एक ऐसी स्त्री के साथ विवाह करता है जिसकी माता वर्णांध तथा पिता सामान्य दृष्टि वाले थे । इस युगल के कितने प्रतिशत पुत्र वर्णांध होंगे ?
questions.text_english: A man whose father was colour-blind marries a woman who had a colour-blind mother and normal father. What percentage of male children of this couple will be colour-blind ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 50%. Colour blindness is an X-linked recessive trait. The man's father was colour-blind, but the man himself has normal vision, so his genotype is X^B Y. The woman's mother was colour-blind (X^b X^b) and father was normal (X^B Y), so the woman is a carrier with genotype X^B X^b. In the cross X^B Y (father) x X^B X^b (mother), the sons receive either X^B (normal) or X^b (colour-blind) from their mother, each with 50% probability. Therefore, 50% of their sons will be colour-blind. Option A (25%) is wrong because it incorrectly calculates from total offspring rather than sons only. Option B (0%) is incorrect as the mother is a carrier. Option D (75%) has no genetic basis for this cross.

questions.text: 'जी ई ए सी' का पूरा नाम है :
questions.text_english: GEAC stands for
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Genetic Engineering Approval Committee. GEAC is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment and Forests, Government of India. It is responsible for approving activities involving large-scale use of hazardous microorganisms and recombinant DNA research in the context of environmental safety, and for approving the release of genetically modified organisms (GMOs) into the environment. Options A, B, and C are incorrect expansions that do not correspond to the actual full form of GEAC.

questions.text: 'कॉलम-A' में दी गई मदों का 'कॉलम-B' में दी गई मदों के साथ समुचित मिलान कीजिए : कॉलम-A: (i) लेडी बर्ड बीटल (भृंग), (ii) माइकोराइजा, (iii) जैविक नियंत्रण, (iv) बायोगैस। कॉलम-B: (a) मीथेनोबैक्टीरियम, (b) ट्राइकोडर्मा, (c) ऐफिड्स, (d) ग्लोमस। उस विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जो कॉलम-A की मदों का कॉलम-B की मदों के साथ सही मिलान करता है।
questions.text_english: Match the items in Column-A with that of Column-B: Column-A: (i) Lady bird beetle, (ii) Mycorrhiza, (iii) Biological control, (iv) Biogas. Column-B: (a) Methanobacterium, (b) Trichoderma, (c) Aphids, (d) Glomus. Choose the option that matches the items of Column A with that of B correctly.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B): (i)-(c), (ii)-(d), (iii)-(b), (iv)-(a). Lady bird beetle feeds on aphids (c), making it a natural predator used in pest control. Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association of fungi with plant roots; Glomus (d) is the most commonly cited mycorrhizal fungus. Trichoderma (b) is a free-living fungus used as a biocontrol agent against several plant pathogens. Biogas is produced by Methanobacterium (a), which is a methanogenic archaebacterium that produces methane during anaerobic decomposition. All other options incorrectly pair one or more items.

questions.text: सूक्ष्मजीवों द्वारा संपादित खनिजीकरण प्रक्रम निम्नलिखित को मुक्त करने में सहायक है :
questions.text_english: The process of mineralization by microorganisms help in the release of :

options.B: अपरद से कार्बनिक तथा अकार्बनिक पोषक दोनों ।
options.D: अपरद से अकाबंनिक पोषक तथा ह्यूमस का बनना ।

options_english.B: both organic and inorganic nutrients from detritus.
options_english.D: inorganic nutrients from detritus and formation of humus.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) inorganic nutrients from detritus and formation of humus. Mineralization is the process carried out by microorganisms on detritus (dead organic matter). During this process, microbes break down the complex organic compounds in detritus and release inorganic nutrients into the soil. As a byproduct of this decomposition, humus (a dark, amorphous substance) is formed which further enriches the soil. Option A is incorrect because inorganic nutrients are released from detritus, not humus. Options B and C are also incorrect in their descriptions of the substrate and products involved.

questions.text: कुछ रोगियों में ऊतक/अंग प्रत्यारोपण अकसर रोगी के ऊतकों/अंगों द्वारा अस्वीकृत किए जाने के कारण असफल हो जाता है । इस प्रकार की अस्वीकृति के लिए उत्तरदायी प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया का प्रकार है :
questions.text_english: Transplantation of tissues/organs to some patients often fails due to rejection of such tissues/organs by the body of the patient. Which type of immune response is responsible for such rejections ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Cell mediated immune response. Organ or tissue transplant rejection is primarily mediated by T-lymphocytes. The recipient's T-cells recognize the foreign MHC (Major Histocompatibility Complex) antigens on the transplanted tissue and mount a cell-mediated immune response, leading to destruction of the transplanted organ. This is why immunosuppressants are given to transplant patients. Autoimmune response (A) refers to the body attacking its own tissues. Humoral immune response (B) involves antibodies produced by B-cells and is not the primary mechanism of graft rejection. Physiological immune response (C) is not a standard immunological term.
questions.topic: Immune system / Graft rejection / Cell-mediated immunity

questions.text: 'कॉलम-I' में दी गई मदों का 'कॉलम-II' में दी गई मदों के साथ समुचित मिलान कीजिए : कॉलम-I: (a) पोषकोरक (ट्रोफोब्लास्ट), (b) अंतरोपण (इम्प्लांटेशन), (c) आन्तर कोशिका पुंज, (d) तूतक (मोरूला)। कॉलम-II: (i) कोरकपुटी का अंत:स्तर (गर्भाशय) में अन्त:स्थापित होना, (ii) कोशिकाओं का समूह जो भ्रूण के रूप में विभेदित हो जाएगा, (iii) 8-16 कोरकखंडों वाला भ्रूण, (iv) कोरकपुटी की बाहरी परत।
questions.text_english: Match the following items of Column-I with that of Column-II: Column-I: (a) Trophoblast, (b) Implantation, (c) Inner cell mass, (d) Morula. Column-II: (i) Embedding of blastocyst in the endometrium, (ii) Group of cells that would differentiate as embryo, (iii) Embryo with 8-16 blastomeres, (iv) Outer layer of blastocyst. Choose the option that matches Column-I with Column-II correctly.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A): (a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iii). Trophoblast (a) is the outer layer of the blastocyst (iv) that helps in implantation and later forms the placenta. Implantation (b) is the process of embedding of the blastocyst in the endometrium (i). The Inner cell mass (c) is the group of cells that will eventually differentiate to form the embryo (ii). Morula (d) is an early embryonic stage consisting of 8-16 blastomeres (iii) formed by repeated cleavage of the zygote. All other options incorrectly match one or more items.

questions.text: नीचे दिए गए चित्र में एक द्विबीजपत्री भ्रूण के विकास के चरणों को दर्शाया गया है । इसके चार भागों को 'P', 'Q', 'R' तथा 'S' द्वारा नामांकित किया गया है । भ्रूण विकास के विभिन्न चरणों में 'P', 'Q', 'R' तथा 'S' के सही नामांकन वाले विकल्प को चुनिए।
questions.text_english: The diagram given below shows labelling of four parts of a dicot embryo during its development as P, Q, R and S. Choose the option that indicates correct labelling of 'P', 'Q', 'R' and 'S' of embryo in different stages of its development.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D): P-Zygote, Q-Suspensor, R-Cotyledon, S-Radicle. In the diagram, P represents the earliest stage which is the Zygote — the single cell formed after fertilization. Q represents the Suspensor, a chain of cells that pushes the embryo into the endosperm for nutrition. R labels the Cotyledon (seed leaf), which is prominent in the mature embryo stage. S labels the Radicle, the embryonic root visible in the heart-shaped embryo stage. Option D correctly identifies all four parts in their developmental sequence. Options A and C are wrong as P is the zygote, not an egg. Options B is wrong because S is radicle, not plumule.

questions.text: डी एन ए पॉलीमरेज का उपयोग करते हुए लाभकारी जीन को लगभग _______ गुना तक प्रवर्धित किया जा सकता है ।
questions.text_english: Amplification of gene of interest by using DNA polymerase may go upto
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 1 billion times. In the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), DNA polymerase (specifically Taq polymerase, a thermostable enzyme) is used to amplify a specific segment of DNA. After approximately 30-35 cycles of denaturation, annealing, and extension, a single copy of the gene of interest can be amplified up to 1 billion (10^9) times. Option A (0.1 million) and B (1 million) are underestimates, while Option D (1 trillion) is an overestimate of the typical amplification achieved by PCR.

questions.text: एक डीएनए खंड की कोडिंग रज्जु में नाइट्रोजनी क्षारकों का अनुक्रम 5' – AATGCTAGGCAC – 3' है । इस डीएनए द्वारा अनुलेखित 'm-आरएनए' में नाइट्रोजनी क्षारकों का सही अनुक्रम दर्शाने वाले विकल्प का चयन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: The sequence of nitrogenous bases in a segment of a coding strand of DNA is 5' – AATGCTAGGCAC – 3'. Choose the option that shows the correct sequence of nitrogenous bases in the mRNA transcribed by the DNA.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 5' – AAUGCUAGGCAC – 3'. The mRNA is transcribed from the template strand, which is complementary and antiparallel to the coding strand. The mRNA sequence is identical to the coding (non-template) strand, except that thymine (T) is replaced by uracil (U). The coding strand is 5'-AATGCTAGGCAC-3', so the mRNA will be 5'-AAUGCUAGGCAC-3'. Option A is wrong as it gives the complementary sequence. Options C and D contain errors in base substitution and are therefore incorrect.

questions.text: एक पुष्पीपादप की लघुबीजाणुधानी के परागकोश की 50 लघुबीजाणु मातृ कोशिकाओं तथा अंडाशय की 50 गुरुबीजाणुधानी मातृ कोशिकाओं से बनने वाले परागकणों तथा बीजाण्डों की संख्या होगी क्रमश:
questions.text_english: How many pollen grains and ovules are likely to be formed in the anther and the ovary of an angiosperm bearing 50 microspore mother cells and 50 megaspore mother cells respectively ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 200, 50. Each microspore mother cell undergoes meiosis to produce 4 microspores (pollen grains). Therefore, 50 microspore mother cells produce 50 x 4 = 200 pollen grains. Each megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis to produce 4 megaspores, but only one functional megaspore survives and develops into the embryo sac (ovule). Therefore, 50 megaspore mother cells produce 50 functional ovules. Option A, C, and D incorrectly apply the division ratio for either pollen or ovule formation.

questions.text: आधुनिक मानव के विकास में निम्नलिखित मानव सदृश्य नर वानर गण (प्राइमेट्स) सम्मिलित हैं । मानव विकास के सही अनुक्रम वाले विकल्प को चुनिए :
questions.text_english: Evolution of modern man involves the following man-like primates. Choose the correct series of human evolution.

options.A: Dryopithecus → Homo erectus → Australopithecines → Homo sapiens
options.B: Australopithecines → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens
options.D: Homo erectus → Australopithecines → Homo sapiens → Neanderthal

options_english.A: Dryopithecus → Homo erectus → Australopithecines → Homo sapiens
options_english.B: Australopithecines → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens
options_english.D: Homo erectus → Australopithecines → Homo sapiens → Neanderthal

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Australopithecines → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens. This represents the accepted sequence of human evolution. Australopithecines (about 2 million years ago) were the first hominids to walk erect. Homo erectus (about 1.5 million years ago) had a larger brain and used fire. Neanderthals (about 1,00,000 years ago) had a large brain and buried their dead. Modern Homo sapiens (about 75,000 years ago) developed language and art. Option A places Homo erectus before Australopithecines which is incorrect. Options C and D have wrong sequences.

questions.text: आरएनए अंतरक्षेप (RNAi) तंबाकू के पौधे को सूत्रकृमि (मेलॉइंडोजिन इनकॉगनीशिया) के प्रति प्रतिरोधी बनाने में सहायक है । उचित विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जिसके द्वारा ज्ञात हो सके कि आरएनए अंतरक्षेपी किस प्रकार प्राप्त किया जाता है :
questions.text_english: RNA interference (RNAi) helps in making tobacco-plant resistant to a nematode (Meloidegyne incognitia). Choose the correct option that shows how RNAi is achieved :

options.A: सूत्रकृमि के एमआरएनए के रूपांतरण प्रक्रम का अवरोधन ।
options.B: सूत्रकृमि के डीएनए के प्रतिकृतीयन को अवरोधित करना ।
options.C: पौधे के डीएनए के अनुलेखन को अवरोधित करना ।
options.D: पौधे के डीएनए के प्रतिकृतीयन को अवरोधित करना ।

options_english.A: Preventing the process of translation of mRNA of the nematode.
options_english.B: Preventing the process of replication of DNA of the nematode.
options_english.C: Preventing the process of transcription of DNA of the plant.
options_english.D: Preventing the process of replication of DNA of the plant.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Preventing the process of translation of mRNA of the nematode. In RNAi-based pest resistance, nematode-specific genes are introduced into the tobacco plant using Agrobacterium tumefaciens. These genes produce complementary dsRNA (double-stranded RNA) in the plant. When the nematode feeds on the plant, this dsRNA enters the nematode cells and silences (prevents translation of) specific nematode mRNA through the RNAi pathway, thereby killing the nematode. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because RNAi acts at the post-transcriptional level by blocking mRNA translation, not by blocking DNA replication or transcription.

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : मुख द्वारा खाई जाने वाली गोली 'सहेली' विश्व की प्रथम गैर-स्टेरॉइडली गर्भनिरोधक गोली है । कारण (R) : इसे राष्ट्रीय प्रतिरक्षा विज्ञान संस्थान, नई दिल्ली द्वारा विकसित किया गया है ।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : Saheli is the World's first non-steroidal oral contraceptive pill. Reason (R) : It has been developed by National Institute of Immunology, New Delhi.
questions.instruction_line: इन प्रश्नों के उत्तर नीचे दिए अनुसार उचित विकल्प को चुनकर दीजिए : (A) (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या हो रही है । (B) (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं हो रही है । (C) (A) सही है, परन्तु (R) गलत है । (D) (A) गलत है, परन्तु (R) सही है ।
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer these questions by selecting the appropriate option: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). (B) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). (C) (A) is true, but (R) is false. (D) (A) is false, but (R) is true.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या हो रही है ।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं हो रही है ।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). Saheli is indeed the world's first non-steroidal oral contraceptive pill containing the compound Centchroman (ormeloxifene). It was developed by scientists at the National Institute of Immunology, New Delhi, under the CSIR program. The Reason correctly explains the Assertion by identifying the institution responsible for developing Saheli. Since both statements are true and the Reason directly explains why Saheli is unique (it was developed at a specific research institution that focused on non-hormonal contraception), option A is correct.

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : आनुवंशिक कूट का एक गुणधर्म इसका अपह्रासित होना है । कारण (R) : कुछ अमीनो अम्ल का कूटलेखन एक से अधिक प्रकूटों द्वारा हो सकता है ।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : One of the property of genetic code is degeneracy. Reason (R) : Some amino acids can be coded by more than one codon.
questions.instruction_line: इन प्रश्नों के उत्तर नीचे दिए अनुसार उचित विकल्प को चुनकर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer these questions by selecting the appropriate option given below.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या हो रही है ।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं हो रही है ।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). Degeneracy of the genetic code means that most amino acids are coded for by more than one codon. For example, the amino acid leucine is coded by six different codons (UUA, UUG, CUU, CUC, CUA, CUG). The Reason directly explains the Assertion: since multiple codons can specify the same amino acid, the code is said to be degenerate. Both statements are factually correct, and R provides the precise molecular basis for the property stated in A.

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : बायोरिएक्टर, वाँछित उत्पाद प्राप्त करने के लिए अनुकूलतम परिस्थितियाँ उपलब्ध करता है । कारण (R) : सर्वाधिक उपयोग किये जाने वाले बायोरिएक्टर विडोलन (स्टिरिंग) प्रकार के हैं ।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : A bioreactor provides the optimal conditions for achieving the desired product by providing optimum growth conditions. Reason (R) : The most commonly used bioreactors are of stirring type.
questions.instruction_line: इन प्रश्नों के उत्तर नीचे दिए अनुसार उचित विकल्प को चुनकर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer these questions by selecting the appropriate option given below.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या हो रही है ।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं हो रही है ।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). The Assertion is correct: a bioreactor is a vessel in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products by microbes, plant or animal cells under optimum conditions of temperature, pH, substrate, salts and vitamins. The Reason is also correct: stirred-tank bioreactors are indeed the most commonly used type in industry. However, the fact that stirring-type reactors are most common does not explain why bioreactors provide optimal conditions — that is because of the precise control of all growth parameters, not specifically because of the stirring mechanism. Hence R does not explain A.

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : एक द्विसंकर क्रॉस में जब दो जीन एक ही क्रोमोसोम पर स्थित होते हैं तो जनकीय जीन संयोजनों का अनुपात अजनकीय प्रकार से काफी ऊँचा रहता है । कारण (R) : जनकीय जीन संयोजनों का अधिक (ऊँचा) होना दो जीनों के विनिमय के कारण हो सकता है ।

options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) (A) is true, but (R) is false. The Assertion is correct: when two genes are located on the same chromosome (linked genes), they tend to be inherited together, so parental combinations are much more frequent than recombinant (non-parental) combinations. This is the phenomenon of linkage. The Reason, however, is false: crossing over does NOT increase parental combinations — it does the opposite by creating recombinant (non-parental) combinations. Crossing over is responsible for the recombinant offspring, not the parental type. The higher frequency of parental combinations is due to linkage, not crossing over.

sub_questions.text_english: How are morphine and heroin related ? Mention their effect on the human body.

key_points: Heroin is derived from morphine by acetylation (chemical modification).
Both depress CNS activity and cause sedation and pain relief.
They are highly addictive and cause dependence.

sub_questions.solution: Morphine is a naturally occurring opiate extracted from the latex of the poppy plant Papaver somniferum. Heroin (diacetylmorphine) is a semi-synthetic drug derived from morphine through a process called acetylation. Both substances act on the central nervous system (CNS), producing strong analgesic (pain-relieving) and sedative effects. They cause euphoria, slowed breathing, and reduced heart rate. Prolonged use leads to tolerance and severe physical and psychological dependence, making withdrawal extremely difficult. Heroin is generally more potent and faster-acting than morphine.

key_points: With distillation: Whisky / Rum / Brandy
Without distillation: Wine / Beer
Cyanobacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen and enrich soil fertility

sub_questions.solution: (i) Alcoholic drinks produced with distillation include whisky, rum, and brandy. Alcoholic drinks produced without distillation include wine and beer, which are produced by fermentation of sugars by yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) alone without further concentration by distillation. (ii) Cyanobacteria such as Anabaena and Nostoc can fix atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia (NH3) through the action of the enzyme nitrogenase. When they grow in paddy fields or are applied as inoculants to the soil, they enrich it with biologically fixed nitrogen, reducing the need for chemical fertilizers and improving soil fertility. Nostoc and Anabaena form symbiotic associations with Azolla, a water fern used as green manure in rice fields.

sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the following ecosystems and discuss, which will be more productive in terms of primary productivity: A young forest, a natural old forest, a shallow polluted lake.

key_points: Young forest has highest primary productivity as most photosynthates go towards growth
Old forest has net productivity near zero as respiration balances photosynthesis
Shallow polluted lake has very low productivity due to pollutants limiting photosynthesis

sub_questions.solution: Among the three ecosystems, a young forest is most productive in terms of primary productivity. A young forest has rapidly growing plants with high rates of photosynthesis and most of the energy fixed goes towards biomass accumulation, giving high net primary productivity. A natural old forest, though having high gross productivity, has a net productivity close to zero because almost all energy fixed by photosynthesis is consumed by the respiration of the large existing biomass. A shallow polluted lake has the lowest productivity because pollutants inhibit photosynthesis and growth of producers, drastically reducing primary productivity.

sub_questions.text: एक पारिस्थितिक-तंत्र की नेट प्राथमिक उत्पादकता तथा सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता के बीच विभेद कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between Net primary productivity and Gross primary productivity in an ecosystem.

key_points: GPP is the total rate of photosynthesis including respiration losses
NPP = GPP minus respiration losses (R)
NPP represents biomass available for consumers

sub_questions.solution: Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is the total amount of organic matter (energy) produced per unit area per unit time through photosynthesis by producers, including the energy used by producers themselves for respiration. Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the organic matter remaining after the autotrophs use up some organic matter in respiration; it equals GPP minus Respiration (R). NPP represents the biomass available to consumers (herbivores) at the next trophic level. While GPP measures total photosynthetic output, NPP is the ecologically more significant measure as it reflects the actual energy available for transfer.

questions.text_english: Study the cross given below : Parents: 44+XY × 44+XX; Gametes: 22+XY, 22+O, 22+X, 22+X; Offsprings: 1, 2. Identify the abnormalities '1' and '2' in the offsprings of a cross done between a couple and distinguish between them.

key_points: Offspring 1 (44+XYY or 44+XXY) - Klinefelter syndrome
Offspring 2 (44+XO) - Turner syndrome
Distinguish by chromosomal constitution, phenotype and symptoms

questions.solution: Offspring '1' is formed by the union of the 22+XY sperm with a 22+X egg, giving 44+XXY. This is Klinefelter Syndrome. The individual is phenotypically male but has underdeveloped testes, feminine features like gynaecomastia, and is sterile. Offspring '2' is formed by the union of the 22+O sperm with a 22+X egg, giving 44+XO. This is Turner Syndrome. The individual is phenotypically female but has underdeveloped ovaries, short stature, webbed neck, and is infertile. The key distinction is: Klinefelter syndrome affects males (XXY, 47 chromosomes) while Turner syndrome affects females (XO, 45 chromosomes).

sub_questions.text_english: A patient with ADA deficiency requires periodic infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes. Explain why such periodic infusion is required and also suggest a permanent cure for such ADA deficiency.

key_points: Infused lymphocytes are not immortal and die after some time, so periodic infusion is needed
Permanent cure: introducing ADA gene into stem cells of bone marrow

sub_questions.solution: ADA (Adenosine Deaminase) deficiency is caused by deletion of the gene for ADA enzyme, which is essential for the immune system to function. Periodic infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes is required because the introduced lymphocytes are not immortal — they have a limited lifespan and eventually die. Once the infused cells die, the patient again loses immune function, necessitating repeated infusions. A permanent cure for ADA deficiency would be to introduce the functional ADA gene into the early embryonic stem cells of the bone marrow using gene therapy. Since stem cells are self-renewing, the correct gene would be propagated in all daughter lymphocytes permanently.

sub_questions.text_english: Describe in brief any two techniques that can be utilised to transfer recombinant DNA into the host cell directly without using any vector.

key_points: Micro-injection: DNA directly injected into nucleus using fine needle
Biolistics/Gene gun: DNA coated gold/tungsten particles bombarded into cells
Electroporation: electric pulse creates pores in cell membrane for DNA entry

sub_questions.solution: Two techniques for directly transferring recombinant DNA into host cells without a vector are: (1) Micro-injection — In this method, recombinant DNA is directly injected into the nucleus of an animal cell using a very fine glass needle (micropipette). This technique is precise and used particularly for animal cells and for producing transgenic animals. (2) Biolistics (Gene gun) — In this method, DNA is coated onto tiny gold or tungsten micro-particles which are then bombarded at high velocity into the target cells using a gene gun. This technique is widely used for transforming plant cells, especially those that are resistant to Agrobacterium-mediated transformation.

questions.text_english: (a) Write the palindromic nucleotide sequence for following sequence of DNA segment : 5' – GAATTC – 3'. (b) Name the restriction endonuclease that recognizes this sequence. (c) How are sticky ends produced ? Mention their role.

key_points: Palindromic sequence: 5'-GAATTC-3' / 3'-CTTAAG-5'
Restriction enzyme: EcoRI
Sticky ends are single-stranded overhangs formed by staggered cuts; they facilitate joining of DNA fragments

questions.solution: (a) A palindromic sequence reads the same on both strands in the 5' to 3' direction. For the given sequence 5'-GAATTC-3', the palindromic double-stranded sequence is: 5'-GAATTC-3' / 3'-CTTAAG-5'. (b) The restriction endonuclease that recognizes the sequence GAATTC is EcoRI (from Escherichia coli). It cuts between G and AATTC on both strands, leaving 4-nucleotide single-stranded overhangs. (c) Sticky ends (cohesive ends) are short single-stranded sequences produced when a restriction enzyme makes staggered cuts on the two strands of the double-stranded DNA rather than straight cuts. Their role is crucial in recombinant DNA technology: the complementary sticky ends of the insert and the vector can hydrogen-bond with each other and are then joined permanently by the enzyme DNA ligase, facilitating the formation of recombinant DNA molecules.

questions.text_english: Study a part of life cycle of Plasmodium given below. Answer the following questions : (a) Name the infective stage of Plasmodium that is stored in the female Anopheles mosquito. (b) Where does fertilization and development of parasite take place ? (c) Identify labels P and Q in the given diagram. (d) Asexual and sexual phase of the life cycle of Plasmodium takes place in two different hosts. Write their names.

key_points: Infective stage: Sporozoites
Fertilization and development occur in the gut of female Anopheles mosquito
P = Sporozoites (stored in salivary glands); Q = Gametocytes
Asexual phase in humans; Sexual phase in female Anopheles mosquito

questions.solution: (a) The infective stage of Plasmodium that is stored in the female Anopheles mosquito is the sporozoite. Sporozoites are stored in the salivary glands of the mosquito and are injected into the human bloodstream during a bite. (b) Fertilization of the parasite (fusion of male and female gametes) and further development into the oocyst takes place in the gut (stomach) of the female Anopheles mosquito. (c) In the diagram, P represents the sporozoites present in the salivary gland of the mosquito, and Q represents the gametocytes (the sexual stage present in the human blood that are taken up by the mosquito). (d) The asexual phase of Plasmodium's life cycle (schizogony) takes place in the human host (primary host), while the sexual phase (gametogony and sporogony) takes place in the female Anopheles mosquito (secondary/vector host).

Justify by taking one example for each. (b) State the importance of the following : (i) IUCN Red data list (ii) Hot spots in conservation of biodiversity

Fragmentation: forest fragmentation reduces population size and gene flow
Habitat loss: deforestation of Amazon causes loss of species
IUCN Red List documents threatened species globally
Hotspots are regions of high endemism prioritized for conservation

questions.solution: (a) Alien species invasion: Introduction of the Nile perch (an exotic predatory fish) into Lake Victoria in Africa led to the extinction of over 200 species of native cichlid fish, disrupting the ecosystem irreversibly. Fragmentation: When large forests are cut into smaller fragments (as in the Amazon), species requiring large territories like tigers and elephants cannot survive, and smaller isolated populations lose genetic diversity and face local extinction. Habitat loss: Destruction of tropical rainforests for agriculture and urbanization has led to the loss of thousands of species, many undiscovered, as seen in Western Ghats and Amazon basin. (b) (i) The IUCN Red Data List is a global inventory that documents the conservation status of plant and animal species, categorizing them as extinct, critically endangered, vulnerable, etc., thereby guiding conservation priorities worldwide. (ii) Biodiversity hotspots are regions that have exceptionally high species richness and high levels of endemism but are also seriously threatened by human activities. Identifying and protecting these regions (e.g., the Western Ghats) ensures maximum biodiversity is conserved per unit conservation effort.
questions.topic: Loss of biodiversity / IUCN Red List / Hotspots

questions.text_english: Study the diagram given below and answer the questions that follows : (a) Identify the structure shown in the above figure. (b) Identify the labels P and Q. (c) Write the nature of histone proteins. (d) Distinguish between Euchromatin and Heterochromatin.

key_points: Structure: Nucleosome
P: DNA double helix; Q: Histone octamer
Histone proteins are positively charged (basic) proteins
Euchromatin: loosely packed, transcriptionally active; Heterochromatin: tightly packed, transcriptionally inactive

questions.solution: (a) The structure shown in the figure is a Nucleosome, which is the fundamental structural unit of chromatin. (b) P represents the DNA double helix (the 2 nm fiber that winds around the protein core), and Q represents the Histone octamer (consisting of two copies each of histones H2A, H2B, H3, and H4). (c) Histone proteins are basic (positively charged) proteins, rich in the positively charged amino acids lysine and arginine. Their positive charge allows them to associate closely with the negatively charged phosphate groups of DNA. (d) Euchromatin is the loosely packed, lightly staining form of chromatin that is transcriptionally active, meaning genes present in euchromatin can be expressed. Heterochromatin is densely packed, darkly staining chromatin that is transcriptionally inactive; the genes in this region are not expressed under normal conditions.

questions.text: श्याम तथा राधा अपनी प्रथम संतान की प्रतीक्षारत हैं क्योंकि राधा दो मास से गर्भवती है और कोई जटिलता भी नहीं है । श्याम के परिवार में पुटीय तंतुमयता का इतिहास है तथा राधा के परिवार में डाउंस सिंड्रोम का पारिवारिक इतिहास है । इसलिए चिंता है कि शिशु को इनमें से कोई एक विकार होने की संभावना है । (a) ऐसे किसी तरीके का सुझाव दीजिए जिससे गर्भस्थ भ्रूण के वंशागत विकार का परीक्षण किया जा सके । उस तकनीक की व्याख्या कीजिए । (b) यदि किसी एक अथवा दोनों विकारों की उपस्थिति पता चलती है तथा माँ के स्वास्थ्य को खतरा हो तो उनके लिए किसी एक संभावित विकल्प का उल्लेख कीजिए । राधा की वर्तमान गर्भावस्था के लिए क्या यह विकल्प सुरक्षित होगा ? न्यायसंगतता सिद्ध कीजिए । (c) किन परिस्थितियों में उप-प्रश्न (b) में सुझाया गया विकल्प अवैधानिक है ?
questions.text_english: Shyam and Radha are expecting their first child with Radha being in her second month of pregnancy with no complications. Shyam's family has a history of cystic fibrosis while Radha's family has a history of Down's syndrome, leading to a concern that the baby may have one of these conditions. (a) Suggest and explain a way of testing if their baby is at risk for any genetic disorders. (b) In case of presence of one or both of the abnormalities and posing a risk to the mother's health, mention one possible option for them to consider. Is that option safe for Radha at the current gestational age ? Justify. (c) Under what conditions is the process mentioned in (b) illegal ?

key_points: Amniocentesis or Chorionic Villi Sampling (CVS) for prenatal diagnosis
MTP (Medical Termination of Pregnancy) is an option; safe up to 20 weeks
MTP is illegal if done for sex determination / after 20 weeks without medical reason

questions.solution: (a) Amniocentesis can be performed to detect genetic disorders in the foetus. In this technique, a small amount of amniotic fluid surrounding the foetus is withdrawn using a needle. Foetal cells present in the fluid are cultured and their chromosomes are analysed for chromosomal abnormalities like Down's syndrome (trisomy 21) and biochemical tests can detect metabolic disorders like cystic fibrosis. (b) If an abnormality is found and the mother's health is at risk, Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) is one possible option. Since Radha is in her second month (approximately 8 weeks), MTP is relatively safe at this stage because the foetus is not yet fully developed. Under the MTP Act, pregnancies up to 20 weeks can be legally terminated, and early termination carries lower medical risks. (c) MTP is illegal under the following conditions: if it is performed for the purpose of sex determination and selective abortion of a female foetus (which is also prohibited under the PCPNDT Act), or if it is carried out without proper medical justification after 20 weeks of gestation, or if it is performed by an unqualified practitioner.

questions.text_english: Explain the basis on which gel electrophoresis technique works. Write any two ways the products obtained through this technique can be utilised.

key_points: DNA fragments migrate through agarose gel under electric current based on size
Smaller fragments migrate faster; larger ones slower
Uses: elution of DNA bands for cloning; DNA fingerprinting / forensic analysis

questions.solution: Gel electrophoresis works on the principle that DNA fragments carry a net negative charge due to their phosphate backbone. When placed in an agarose gel matrix and subjected to an electric field, these negatively charged fragments migrate towards the positive electrode (anode). Smaller fragments encounter less resistance from the gel matrix and therefore migrate faster and travel further, while larger fragments migrate more slowly and remain closer to the point of origin. This results in separation of DNA fragments based on their size. The separated fragments appear as bands, visible under UV light after staining with ethidium bromide. Two uses of the products obtained: (1) Individual bands can be cut out from the gel and the DNA can be eluted (extracted) for use in further molecular procedures such as cloning into vectors. (2) The banding pattern obtained is used in DNA fingerprinting for forensic applications such as identification of criminals, paternity testing, and identification of disaster victims.

questions.text_english: Compare and contrast convergent and divergent evolution.

key_points: Divergent: common ancestry, different forms/functions due to different environments — homologous organs
Convergent: different ancestry, similar forms/functions due to similar environments — analogous organs
Examples: Divergent — forelimbs of vertebrates; Convergent — wings of bat and insect

questions.solution: Divergent evolution refers to the process where organisms with a common ancestor evolve different characteristics over time due to adaptation to different environments or ecological niches. It results in the formation of homologous organs — structures that have the same basic anatomy and embryonic origin but perform different functions, such as the forelimbs of a whale, bat, human, and cheetah. Convergent evolution, on the other hand, refers to the process where organisms from different ancestral lineages independently evolve similar structures or traits due to adaptation to similar environments or lifestyles. It results in the formation of analogous organs — structures that have different embryonic origins but perform similar functions, such as the wings of a butterfly and the wings of a bird, or the streamlined body shape of a dolphin and a shark.
questions.topic: Convergent and divergent evolution / Analogous and homologous organs

sub_questions.text_english: Which hormone is responsible for the peak observed in Case 1 and Case 2 ? Write one function of that hormone.

key_points: Hormone responsible for peak: LH (Luteinizing Hormone)
Function: LH surge triggers ovulation

sub_questions.solution: The hormone responsible for the peak observed in both Case 1 and Case 2 is Luteinizing Hormone (LH). The sharp LH surge (peak) that occurs just before ovulation is the stimulus that triggers the rupture of the mature Graafian follicle and the release of the ovum (ovulation). One important function of LH is to induce ovulation and stimulate the ruptured follicle to develop into the corpus luteum, which then secretes progesterone to prepare the uterus for implantation.

sub_questions.text_english: Write changes that take place in the ovary and uterus during follicular phase.

key_points: Ovary: primary follicles develop into Graafian follicles under FSH stimulation
Uterus: endometrium regenerates and thickens under oestrogen influence

sub_questions.solution: During the follicular phase, several changes occur in the ovary and uterus. In the ovary, under the influence of Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH), primary follicles grow and develop into mature Graafian follicles. These follicles secrete increasing amounts of oestrogen. In the uterus, the rising levels of oestrogen cause the endometrium (uterine lining) to proliferate and thicken in preparation for potential implantation. The endometrial glands regenerate, and blood supply to the uterine lining increases.

sub_questions.text_english: Name the hormone Q of Case 2. Write one function of hormone Q.

key_points: Hormone Q in Case 2 is HCG (Human Chorionic Gonadotropin)
Function: maintains corpus luteum during early pregnancy

sub_questions.solution: The hormone Q in Case 2 is HCG (Human Chorionic Gonadotropin). In Case 2, the graph shows the presence of HCG rising during the luteal phase, indicating a pregnancy scenario. One important function of HCG is that it is secreted by the trophoblast of the developing embryo after implantation. HCG maintains the corpus luteum and stimulates it to continue secreting progesterone and oestrogen during early pregnancy, preventing menstruation and supporting the developing embryo until the placenta takes over hormone production.

key_points: Corpus luteum remains functional in Case 2 (pregnancy)
It is formed from the ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation under the influence of LH

sub_questions.solution: In Case 2 (which represents pregnancy, as indicated by the presence of HCG), the corpus luteum will remain functional throughout early pregnancy. After ovulation, the ruptured Graafian follicle is stimulated by LH to transform into the corpus luteum — a temporary endocrine structure that forms from the remnants of the follicular wall and its cells. The granulosa and theca cells of the follicle undergo luteinization (enlargement, lipid accumulation, and yellowish appearance) to form the corpus luteum. In Case 2, HCG secreted by the implanted embryo prevents the degeneration of the corpus luteum, allowing it to continue secreting progesterone to maintain the pregnancy.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित परिच्छेद को पढ़कर अग्रगामी प्रश्नों के उत्तर लिखिए : प्रकृति में, हमें किसी भी जाति के पृथक, एकल व्यष्टि के दर्शन विरले ही होते हैं; उनमें से अधिकांश सुपरिभाषित भौगोलिक क्षेत्र में समूह में रहते हैं । वे समान संसाधनों का साझा उपयोग करते हैं अथवा उनके लिए स्पर्धा करते हैं, संकरण करते हैं और इस प्रकार वे समष्टि की रचना करते हैं । समष्टि में कुछ ऐसे गुण होते हैं जो व्यष्टि जीव में नहीं होते । एक नियत समय में समष्टि में विभिन्न आयु वर्ग की व्यष्टियाँ होती हैं । किसी समष्टि का आकार उसके आवास में समष्टि की स्थिति के बारे में बहुत कुछ बताता है । समष्टि में हम कैसे भी पारिस्थितिक प्रक्रम अन्वेषण (इन्वेस्टिगेट) करना चाहें, भले ही यह दूसरी जातियों में स्पर्धा का परिणाम हो, परभक्षी का प्रभाव हो, या पीड़कनाशी (पेस्टीसाइड) अनुप्रयुक्त करने का प्रभाव हो, हम उनका मूल्यांकन हमेशा ही समष्टि के साइज में परिवर्तन के संदर्भ में करते हैं । प्रकृति में समष्टि का आकार (साइज) बहुत कम हो सकता है अथवा लाखों की संख्या में हो सकता है । समष्टि का आकार (साइज) तकनीकी रूप से समष्टि घनत्व (N) कहलाता है । परन्तु यह आवश्यक नहीं है कि इसे केवल संख्या के आधार पर ही मापा जाए । किसी समष्टि के लिए समष्टि का साइज एक निश्चल (स्थिर) प्राचल नहीं है । यह समय के साथ परिवर्तित होता रहता है जो अनेक कारकों भोजन की उपलब्धता, परभक्षण दाब तथा विपरीत मौसम पर निर्भर करता है ।
questions.text_english:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow :

In nature, we rarely find isolated, single individuals of any species; majority of them live in groups in a well-defined geographical area, share or compete for similar resources, potentially interbreed and thus constitute a population. The population has certain attributes whereas, an individual organism does not. A population at a given time is composed of individuals of different ages. The size of the population tells us a lot about its status in the habitat. Whatever ecological processes we wish to investigate in a population, be it the outcome of competition with another species, the impact of the predator or the effect of pesticide application, we always evaluate in terms of any change in the population size. The size, in nature, could be low or go into millions. Population size, technically called population density (N) need not necessarily be measured in numbers only. The size of a population for any species is not a static parameter. It keeps on changing with time depending on various factors including food availability, predation pressure and adverse weather.

sub_questions.text_english: The Monarch butterfly is highly distasteful to its predator because of a special chemical present in its body. How does the butterfly acquire this chemical ?

key_points: The Monarch butterfly acquires the chemical by feeding on milkweed plants during its larval (caterpillar) stage

sub_questions.solution: The Monarch butterfly acquires the special distasteful chemical (a toxic cardiac glycoside) by feeding on milkweed plants (Asclepias) during its larval (caterpillar) stage. The caterpillars sequester these toxic chemicals from the milkweed into their bodies. These chemicals are retained through metamorphosis into the adult butterfly and make the Monarch highly unpalatable and toxic to its predators such as birds. This is an example of chemical defence and mimicry in ecology.

sub_questions.text: यदि किसी जाति का समष्टि घनत्व एक समय t + 1 = 800, उत्प्रवासन = 100, आप्रवासन = 200, जन्मदर = 200 तथा मृत्युदर = 150 है, तो उस समय 't' पर समष्टि दर का परिकलन कीजिए तथा इस केस में बनने वाले आयु पिरेमिड के प्रकार पर समीक्षा (टिप्पणी) कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: If population density at a time t + 1 is 800, Emigration = 100, Immigration = 200, Natality = 200 and Mortality = 150, calculate the population density at time t and comment upon the type of age pyramid that will be formed in this case.

key_points: Since birth rate > death rate, population is growing; expanding/pyramid-shaped age pyramid

sub_questions.solution: Using the population growth formula: N(t+1) = N(t) + (B - D) + (I - E), where B = Natality, D = Mortality, I = Immigration, E = Emigration. Substituting values: 800 = N(t) + (200 - 150) + (200 - 100) = N(t) + 50 + 100 = N(t) + 150. Therefore, N(t) = 800 - 150 = 650. The population density at time t was 650. Since birth rate (200) is greater than death rate (150) and immigration (200) is greater than emigration (100), the population is growing. This growing population will form an expanding (pyramid-shaped) age pyramid with a broad base (large pre-reproductive class), indicating a young and growing population.

sub_questions.text: किसी क्षेत्र में 200 गाजर घास वाले पौधों तथा केवल एक विशालकाय बरगद के वृक्ष के समष्टि घनत्व को मापने की विधि में क्या अंतर है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What is the difference in a method of measuring population density in an area if there are 200 carrot grass plants to only single huge banyan tree ?

key_points: For carrot grass: measured by counting numbers (numerical density)
For banyan tree: measured by biomass or percentage cover, not numbers, as a single tree covers vast area

sub_questions.solution: For the 200 carrot grass (Parthenium) plants, population density can be measured by direct counting of individuals (numerical density) since the plants are small and countable. However, for the single huge banyan tree, measuring population density simply by numbers (N=1) would be misleading and uninformative about its ecological impact, since one banyan tree can have an enormous canopy covering a very large area and contribute far more biomass. In such cases, population density of the banyan tree should be measured by its percentage cover (the proportion of ground area covered by its canopy) or by its biomass, which gives a more ecologically meaningful measure of its abundance and impact on the habitat.

sub_questions.text: बाघ की समष्टि घनत्व के मापन की दो विधियों (तरीकों) के नाम लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Name two methods to measure the population density of tigers.

key_points: Pug mark census (counting paw prints)
Camera trap method

sub_questions.solution: Two methods used to measure the population density of tigers are: (1) Pug mark census — In this traditional method, the paw prints (pugmarks) of tigers are collected from the field, and each individual tiger's pug marks are identified and counted based on their unique shape and size. This gives an estimate of the number of tigers in the area. (2) Camera trap method — Camera traps (motion-triggered cameras) are placed across the habitat. Tigers are individually identified from their unique stripe patterns captured in photographs. The number of individual tigers photographed gives an estimate of population density. This method is now preferred over the pug mark method for its accuracy.

sub_questions.text_english: (i) What is MALT? Where is it located? (ii) Explain cytokine barriers. (iii) Name the diagnostic test for AIDS and its principle. (iv) Role of bone marrow and thymus in immune system.

key_points: MALT: Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue, located in digestive, respiratory, urogenital tracts
Cytokine barriers: virus-infected cells secrete interferons that protect neighboring cells
AIDS test: ELISA based on antigen-antibody interaction
Bone marrow: site of origin and maturation of B-cells; Thymus: site of T-cell maturation

sub_questions.solution: (i) MALT stands for Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue. It constitutes about 50% of the lymphoid tissue in the human body and is located in the lining of the major tracts such as the digestive tract, respiratory tract, and the urogenital tract. It provides immune surveillance at these mucosal surfaces. (ii) Cytokine barriers (Interferons): When a cell is infected by a virus, it releases small proteins called interferons. These interferons diffuse to neighboring uninfected cells and stimulate them to produce antiviral proteins that inhibit viral replication, thereby protecting cells surrounding the infection site. This constitutes a cytokine barrier against viral spread. (iii) The diagnostic test for AIDS is ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay). It works on the principle of antigen-antibody interaction. It detects the presence of HIV-specific antibodies in the patient's serum, indicating exposure to the HIV virus. (iv) Bone marrow is the primary lymphoid organ where all blood cells, including lymphocytes (B-cells and T-cells), are produced from haematopoietic stem cells. B-cells also mature in the bone marrow. The thymus is a primary lymphoid organ located in the chest where T-lymphocytes undergo maturation, differentiation, and are selected for self-tolerance, before being released into the bloodstream as immunocompetent T-cells.

(ii) Baculoviruses (particularly Nucleopolyhedrovirus) are used as biological control agents because they are species-specific pathogens — they attack and kill only the target insect pest species and have no adverse effects on non-target organisms such as plants, mammals, birds, fish, and beneficial insects like bees. They are therefore narrow-spectrum, environment-friendly biocontrol agents that can be used as alternatives to chemical pesticides in integrated pest management programmes.

sub_questions.text_english: (a) Distinguish between two cells in mature male gametophyte. (b) Questions on pollination methods.

key_points: Vegetative/tube cell and Generative cell differ in size, nucleus, and function
Method 1: Autogamy; Method 2: Geitonogamy; Method 3: Xenogamy
Water lily: entomophily (insect pollination); Vallisneria: hydrophily (water pollination)
Xenogamy advantages: genetic variation, hybrid vigour

sub_questions.solution: (a) The mature male gametophyte (pollen grain) of an angiosperm contains two cells: the Vegetative cell (tube cell) and the Generative cell. The vegetative cell is larger, has an irregular nucleus, and is metabolically active. It forms the pollen tube. The generative cell is smaller, spindle-shaped, with a dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus. It divides mitotically to produce two male gametes (sperm cells). (b)(i) From the diagram, Method 1 appears to show cross-pollination between flowers of different plants (Xenogamy), Method 2 shows pollination between different flowers on the same plant (Geitonogamy), and Method 3 shows self-pollination within the same flower (Autogamy). (ii) (a) Water lily achieves pollination through insects (entomophily) — insects are attracted to its large, colourful flowers and transfer pollen while visiting for nectar. (b) Vallisneria achieves pollination through water (hydrophily) — the male flowers detach and float to the surface, where they come in contact with female flowers that have been raised to the water surface by elongating stalks. (iii) Advantages of Method '3' (Xenogamy/cross-pollination): It brings together genetic material from two different plants, leading to genetic recombination, greater genetic variability, and the production of hybrid offspring with increased vigour (heterosis), better adaptability, and resistance to diseases.

sub_questions.text: (i) शुक्राणु P, Q, R के प्रारब्ध की तुलना। (ii) जोना पेलुसिडा की भूमिका। (iii) शुक्राणु प्रविष्टि के बाद परिवर्तन। (iv) अग्रपिंडक और मध्यखंड की भूमिका।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Compare fate of sperms P, Q, R. (ii) Role of Zona pellucida. (iii) Changes in ovum after sperm entry. (iv) Role of acrosome and middle piece.

key_points: P: inside zona pellucida, likely to fertilize; Q: penetrating zona pellucida; R: outside, cannot fertilize
Zona pellucida: species-specific sperm recognition and block to polyspermy
Cortical reaction, completion of meiosis II, formation of fertilization membrane
Acrosome releases enzymes to penetrate zona pellucida; middle piece provides energy via mitochondria

sub_questions.solution: (i) Sperm P, which is shown inside or has passed through the zona pellucida, will succeed in fertilizing the ovum. Sperm Q, shown penetrating the zona pellucida, is in the process of making its way in but will be blocked after P fertilizes the egg due to the zona reaction. Sperm R, which is outside the zona pellucida, will not be able to fertilize the ovum as the zona reaction following P's entry will prevent additional sperm from penetrating. (ii) The zona pellucida plays a crucial role in fertilization: it contains species-specific sperm receptors (ZP3 glycoprotein) that allow only sperm of the same species to bind. After one sperm has fused with the ovum, the zona pellucida undergoes a chemical change (zona reaction) that hardens and creates a block to polyspermy, preventing additional sperm from entering. (iii) After entry of the sperm, the following changes occur in the ovum: the secondary oocyte (which was arrested in Meiosis II) completes its second meiotic division to form the mature ovum and the second polar body. The fusion of the sperm and ovum nuclei (syngamy) forms the diploid zygote. Cortical granules beneath the plasma membrane are released (cortical reaction), causing the zona pellucida to harden and form the fertilization membrane, preventing polyspermy. (iv) The acrosome, present at the tip of the sperm head, contains hydrolytic enzymes (acrosin, hyaluronidase). These enzymes are released upon contact with the zona pellucida (acrosomal reaction) and digest a path through the zona pellucida, enabling the sperm to penetrate and reach the ovum for fertilization. The middle piece of the sperm is densely packed with mitochondria arranged spirally. These mitochondria provide the energy (in the form of ATP) required for vigorous flagellar movement of the sperm tail, enabling the sperm to swim through the female reproductive tract to reach the ovum.

key_points: Cross HbA HbS x HbA HbS; F1: 1 normal : 2 carrier : 1 diseased
Nitrogenous base: Adenine substituted by Thymine (A to T transversion / glutamic acid replaced by valine)
Pea: complete dominance (3:1 ratio); Snapdragon: incomplete dominance (1:2:1 ratio with pink intermediate)

sub_questions.solution: (i) Cross between two sickle cell carriers (Hb^A Hb^S × Hb^A Hb^S): F1 progeny — Hb^A Hb^A (1 disease-free/normal) : Hb^A Hb^S (2 carriers) : Hb^S Hb^S (1 diseased/sickle cell anaemia patient). The ratio of disease-free : carrier : diseased is 1:2:1. In sickle cell anaemia, in the beta-globin gene, the codon GAG is changed to GTG due to a point mutation in which Adenine is substituted by Thymine. This leads to the replacement of the amino acid Glutamic acid by Valine in the haemoglobin beta chain, causing the HbS molecule. (ii) In garden pea (Pisum sativum), flower colour shows complete dominance. In a cross between red-flowered (RR) and white-flowered (rr) plants, the F1 is all red (Rr) showing complete dominance. F2 gives a 3 red : 1 white ratio. In snapdragon (Antirrhinum majus), flower colour shows incomplete dominance. A cross between red-flowered (R^1R^1) and white-flowered (R^2R^2) plants gives F1 pink-flowered (R^1R^2) plants, because neither allele is completely dominant over the other, and the intermediate pink phenotype is expressed. F2 gives a 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white ratio (1:2:1 genotypic and phenotypic ratio coincide). This demonstrates that in snapdragon, the phenotypic ratio in F2 is different from the 3:1 ratio seen in pea, due to the blending of traits in the heterozygote.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain with the help of well-labelled diagrams how lac operon operates in E. coli: (i) In presence of an inducer. (ii) In absence of an inducer.

key_points: Absence of inducer: repressor binds operator, RNA polymerase blocked, structural genes not transcribed
Presence of inducer (lactose/allolactose): inducer binds repressor, repressor cannot bind operator, RNA polymerase transcribes lacZ, lacY, lacA
Products: beta-galactosidase, permease, transacetylase

sub_questions.solution: The lac operon in E. coli is a set of three structural genes (lacZ, lacY, lacA) under the control of a common promoter and operator, regulated by a repressor protein encoded by the regulatory gene (lacI). (i) In the presence of an inducer (lactose or its isomer allolactose): The inducer molecule binds to the repressor protein and changes its shape (allosteric change), making it unable to bind to the operator sequence. With the operator free, RNA polymerase binds to the promoter and transcribes the structural genes lacZ, lacY, and lacA into a polycistronic mRNA. This mRNA is translated to produce the enzymes beta-galactosidase (breaks down lactose), permease (transports lactose into cell), and transacetylase. Thus, when lactose is available, the operon is switched ON to metabolise it. (ii) In the absence of an inducer (no lactose): The repressor protein produced by the lacI gene is in its active form and binds tightly to the operator sequence. This physically blocks RNA polymerase from moving along the DNA and transcribing the structural genes. As a result, the structural genes are not transcribed and no enzymes for lactose metabolism are produced. The operon is switched OFF, conserving cellular resources when lactose is not present. Well-labelled diagrams should show: regulatory gene, promoter, operator, structural genes, repressor in both active (bound to operator) and inactive (bound to inducer) states.
